blocks.body: 'No space left' with free disk = inodes exhausted (df -i). 'Too many open files' = ulimit/nofile. Know both failure modes.
kubectl describe pod → events: unschedulable (resources, taints, affinity, PVC unbound). Fix the constraint, not the pod.
logs --previous → bad image/entrypoint, missing env/secret, failed probe. describe shows the event trail.
Container exceeded memory limit. Raise limits after profiling, or fix the leak — don't just raise blindly.
Node pressure (disk/memory). Check node allocatable vs requests; set proper requests/limits.
Declarative, state-tracked, plan-before-apply. Strengths: multi-cloud, modules, drift detection. Weaknesses: state management, imperative gaps.
Agentless, procedural-when-needed, idempotent tasks. Strengths: config management, low friction. Weaknesses: scale, ordering complexity.
Terraform provisions the platform; Ansible configures the hosts. Import for drifted resources; for_each over count; modules for reuse; secrets never in state committed.
Commit → build/test/SAST → artifact → stage (DAST) → prod (canary) → observe. Gates block on failures, CVEs, secrets.
Jenkins: Groovy shared libraries, self-hosted control. GitHub Actions/Azure DevOps: YAML, OIDC, managed runners. Know both; argue fit.
Azure: VNet, Private Link, AKS node pools. AWS: VPC, IAM, EKS. GCP: global VPC, GKE. Private DNS + Private Link patterns recur.
Narrate the model, do the math (SLO budgets, capacity), name the tradeoff, verify. No copilot — the reps make it automatic.

studyGuide.title: Study guide: how to work this course

plan: Phase 1 — Foundations, M01-M06 (~50 h): math for infrastructure; drill until green before touching Linux.
Phase 2 — Linux & networking, M07-M15: live in the terminal; every lab runs for real on your machine.
Phase 3 — Containers & orchestration, M16-M31: Docker then Kubernetes; the triage runbooks are the job.
Phase 4 — IaC & CI/CD, M32-M39: Terraform and Ansible back-to-back; build the chain labs in order.
Phase 5 — Clouds & production, M40-M49: Azure first, then AWS/GCP; observability and DevSecOps gates.
Phase 6 — Interview simulation, M50: cold answers only. Record yourself; no copilot, no notes.

rules: Drills to green before the next module.
One tool-install lab per tool, before its module.
Score every mock task; re-take below 80%.

timeFormula: estimatedMinutes per module = weight x 120 + notes x 12 + cards x 4 + quiz x 8 + drill items x 4 + handsOnLab 90 + min(180, videoMinutes/2). Course total = sum of module estimates.

glossary.definition: Filesystem metadata entry per file; exhaustion blocks writes despite free bytes.
Per-process handle for open files/sockets; ulimit caps them.
Init + service manager: units, journald, systemctl.
Mandatory access control via contexts; the RHEL troubleshooter's reflex check.
Cloud-isolated networks: subnets, route tables, security groups/NSGs.
Private connectivity to cloud services without public internet exposure.
K8s: container repeatedly crashing on start — check logs --previous and events.
Container killed for exceeding memory limits (exit 137).
The config→reality mapping; remote, locked, per-environment.
Reality diverging from IaC — detected by plan, fixed by import or revert.
Reliability target and its allowed unreliability; the shipping policy lever.
Static (code) and dynamic (running app) security testing gates.
Signed artifacts, SBOMs, provenance: trusting the pipeline's inputs.
Grouped VM sets backing AKS clusters; autoscale per pool.
The course's timed no-copilot exam: every BNY DevOps panel question, answered independently.

faq.q: How is IL-28 different from IL-05?
faq.a: IL-05 is the certification-depth platform track. IL-28 is the production bootcamp: math → Linux → networking → containers → IaC → CI/CD → multicloud → observability/security, calibrated to a real hiring panel (BNY DevOps). IL-28 is the 'answer everything independently' course.

A timed simulation of the actual panel loop: infrastructure math, Linux troubleshooting, cloud networking, K8s triage, IaC tradeoffs, CI/CD design — no copilot, narrated aloud. It's the course's graduation gate.
The target environments (and panel) are RHEL-family: SELinux, systemd depth, RHEL troubleshooting patterns. Skills transfer to Debian-family; the panel tests RHEL.
Terraform for provisioning (it's the panel's IaC default), Ansible for configuration. The course teaches both and makes you argue the tradeoffs — that's the scored skill.

faq.q: How do I practice K8s triage without a cluster?
faq.a: kind/k3d locally: deliberately break things (bad images, low limits, unbound PVCs) and triage them. The course's triage cheat sheet is the checklist; the reps build the reflex.

tips: Follow the guided path in order — each module unlocks the next. The sequence is the curriculum; skipping ahead breaks the chain.

This course maps to HashiCorp Terraform Associate (004) and CKA / CKAD concepts (Kubernetes) (independent preparation — no affiliation). Weight your drill time toward the heaviest exam domains shown in the cert gates.

The math modules (Boolean Algebra & Digital Logic, Set Theory & Access Logic, Modular Arithmetic & Cryptography Foundations) are load-bearing — finish them before the applied modules that assume them.
Quiz-gated modules need 70%+ to unlock the next. When you miss a question, ask Noah to walk you through the miss Socratically before re-attempting.
Do each hands-on lab twice — once following the guide, once from a blank screen. The second pass is where the skill sticks.
This is a 473-hour course: at 10 focused hours a week it takes about 12 months. Short daily sessions beat weekend cramming — pace it like a semester.
